answers.answer:
SCOPe family membership rests on a shared structural and evolutionary unit, not on matching chain length. In release 2.08 (current public release, periodic update 2026-08-16), all three domains are in a.298.1.1. d2kq5a_ (2kq5 A:) is under protein PthA, species Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri. d3v6pa_ (3v6p A:) is dHax3, an engineered TALE from Xanthomonas. d4cj9a_ (4cj9 A:) is BurrH from Burkholderia rhizoxinica. The seqres lengths returned by the API are 51, 373 and 752 residues.

The length difference is mostly a repeat-count and construct effect. TAL effector DNA-binding domains are built from tandem repeats of about 34 residues. Each repeat is a two-helix hairpin, and the hypervariable repeat-variable diresidue (RVD) sits at positions 12–13 of each repeat. The repeats stack into a right-handed superhelix. d2kq5a_ is only a ~51-residue fragment, about 1.5 repeats (the sequence shows the QVVAIAS-HD-GGKQALETVQRLLPVLCQAHG motif twice). d3v6pa_ has roughly 11 repeats (373 residues), and the sequence shows the same repeating motif with different RVDs (HD, NG, NS, NI and others). d4cj9a_ has about 20 repeats (752 residues), and its repeats are more divergent than the Xanthomonas ones. SCOPe classifies the domain as the repeat unit and its structural motif, so a fragment, a medium array and a long array fall in one family. Adding or removing repeats does not change the family assignment. The domain boundaries also depend on which residues were resolved in the PDB entry. This is why repeat proteins like this one show vastly different lengths within one family.

Limits on interpretation:
- Family placement means a common ancestry and the same repeat architecture. It does not mean similar length, similar sequence, or similar function.
- The Xanthomonas TALE/PthA/dHax3 repeats are close to each other. BurrH (Burkholderia) is a more distant homolog with more divergent repeats, and it is grouped through the shared repeat fold and the family-level relationship SCOPe curates.
- Sequence identity within a repeat array is high between repeats of one protein, so pairwise global alignment or percent identity between a 51-residue fragment and a 752-residue protein is misleading.
- Do not transfer DNA-target specificity from one entry to another. Specificity depends on the RVD at each repeat, so it must be read repeat by repeat. d2kq5a_ is a short fragment, d3v6pa_ is an engineered dHax3 construct, and BurrH has a different repeat array and N-terminal region. None of them can be treated as a template for another's binding site, repeat count or biological function.
- Choose representatives or templates by repeat count, RVD content and the intended use, not by family label alone.
- I did not retrieve any external evidence beyond the SCOPe API (no literature, PDB or DNA-binding data), so the repeat-length and RVD details come from the returned sequences and from background knowledge of TALE structure. I did not verify the fold and superfamily names above family level (a.298.x), so I make no claim about them.
